subject: Maths
subtopic: Area of trapeziums and composite shapes
title: Area of trapeziums and composite shapes
subtitle: Area and Perimeter · KS3 Maths
learning_objective: I can calculate the area of trapeziums and composite shapes by splitting into simpler shapes.

key_vocab.definition: A trapezium has one pair of parallel sides (a and b). Its area is &frac{1}{2}(a + b) × h.

sections.title: Learning Objective
sections.content: I can calculate the area of trapeziums and composite shapes by splitting into simpler shapes.

sections.title: Key Words
sections.content: trapezium -- A trapezium has one pair of parallel sides (a and b). Its area is &frac{1}{2}(a + b) × h.

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
Trapezium: average the parallel sides, then multiply by the height.
A = &frac{1}{2}(a + b) × h
Average of parallel sides times height

Key examples:
  ✓ Trapezium: A = &frac{1}{2}(a + b)h  (parallel sides a, b)
  ✓ Composite: split into known shapes  (then add areas)
  ✓ a = 5, b = 9, h = 4 → A = 28  (&frac{1}{2}(14)×4)
  ✗ Trapezium: A = a × b × h  (wrong formula)
  ✗ Composite: just add all lengths  (that gives perimeter)

sections.title: Worked Example
sections.content:
Example 1 – basic trapezium
  A trapezium has parallel sides 6 cm and 10 cm, height 4 cm. Find the area.
  A = &frac{1}{2}(a + b) × h
  A = &frac{1}{2}(6 + 10) × 4 = &frac{1}{2} × 16 × 4
  A = 32 cm²
  = 32 cm²
  (Add the parallel sides, halve, then multiply by height.)

Example 2 – finding height
  A trapezium has area 30 cm², parallel sides 4 cm and 8 cm. Find h.
  30 = &frac{1}{2}(4 + 8) × h
  30 = 6h
  h = 5 cm
  h = 5 cm
  (Rearrange: h = A ÷ &frac{1}{2}(a + b).)

sections.title: Trapezium area
sections.content:
Find the area of each trapezium.

(a) a = 5 cm, b = 9 cm, h = 4 cm
(b) a = 3 cm, b = 7 cm, h = 6 cm
(c) a = 8 cm, b = 12 cm, h = 5 cm
(d) a = 4 cm, b = 10 cm, h = 3 cm

sections.title: Finding missing measurements
sections.content:
Use the formula to find the missing value.

(a) A = 24, a = 4, b = 8. Find h.
(b) A = 35, a = 3, h = 5. Find b.
(c) A = 40, b = 12, h = 4. Find a.
(d) A = 27, a = 5, b = 4. Find h.

sections.title: L-shapes and U-shapes
sections.content:
Find the area of each composite shape.

(a) L-shape: 10×8, cut-out 4×5
(b) L-shape: 12×6, cut-out 3×3
(c) U-shape: 8×6, cut-out 4×3 (centre)
(d) L-shape: 9×7, cut-out 5×4

sections.title: T-shapes and plus signs
sections.content:
Split into rectangles, then add.

(a) T-shape: top 8×2, stem 3×5
(b) T-shape: top 12×3, stem 4×6
(c) Plus: 10×2 and 2×10 overlap 2×2
(d) Arrow: rectangle 6×4 + triangle b=6, h=3

sections.title: Mixed composite and trapezium
sections.content:
Find each area.

(a) Trapezium: a = 6, b = 14, h = 8
(b) Composite: rectangle 5×10 + triangle b=5, h=4
(c) Trapezium: a = 7, b = 11, h = 6
(d) L-shape: 15×10, cut-out 8×6
(e) Pentagon (split): rectangle 8×5 + triangle b=8, h=3

sections.title: Common Mistakes
sections.content:
✓ Trapezium area = &frac{1}{2}(a + b) × h
✗ Composite area: add all the sides together
✓ Split composite shapes into rectangles and triangles
✗ Trapezium area = a × b × h
✓ For an L-shape, subtract the cut-out from the full rectangle
